title: 5-turn tactical CCG with blind placement, 2-of-3 win conditions and a daily roguelite mode. Solo dev, free demo on Steam.
author: ValhallaArchiveCCG
selftext:
🔗 [https://store.steampowered.com/app/5289190/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5289190/)

Solo dev, built after my day job over \~a year. Free demo just went live on Steam, and I want to share how AI actually fit into the work — including where it didn't.

**Art:** all card art is AI-generated, then hand-curated. Keeping 100 cards in one visual style was the hard part — most generations were rejected for style drift, not quality. I never touched a paintbrush; curation was the job.

**Code:** Claude as a pair programmer in Unity + PlayFab. I own the architecture, rules and balance; it wrote most of the boilerplate, the server-side CloudScript handlers, and the tooling around them. Two lessons:

* It passed syntax checks and still shipped a server deploy where every handler failed at runtime (a scoping bug across files). Now every deploy runs a smoke harness that executes all handlers before upload. "It compiles" means nothing.
* Best use was tooling, not features: a 10-language localization pipeline with per-language QA scripts (French non-breaking spaces, Russian case agreement, German compounds) that I could never have justified building by hand.

**The game:** blind placement — both players set cards face-down at once, then everything flips. A random rift then hits the board (slots collapse, mana shifts, slots lock). Win 2 of 3: card count, total power, board mana, in exactly 5 turns. Plus card crafting, a 100-floor tower (30 in demo) and a daily roguelite "corridor" run. 100 cards, 10 languages.

Happy to answer workflow questions — and honest feedback on whether the 5-turn limit feels tense or just random is welcome.
